raw.description:
About HappyRobot

HappyRobot is the infrastructure for enterprises to build and orchestrate AI workforces. Our AI workers don't just communicate through voice and email - they make decisions, take action, and run operations autonomously across entire enterprise systems. Born in Y Combinator (S23) and backed by a16z, Base10, Prysm Capital and Eurazeo with over $150M raised, we power critical operations for global enterprises worldwide.

Our platform is battle-tested in the most demanding environments, where AI has real consequences. We started in logistics, built our own voice stack, models, and orchestration layer from the ground up, and are now bringing that infrastructure to every enterprise that runs the real economy. Learn more about our vision in our manifesto.

Role Overview

We are looking for a versatile and highly skilled German-speaking Forward Deployed Engineer to join our team. In this role, you will combine strong technical abilities with excellent communication skills, working directly with customers to ensure they maximize the value of HappyRobot’s AI platform. You will be involved in onboarding, implementation, and ongoing support, while also contributing to product development and innovation.


At HappyRobot, there’s no role seniority or hierarchy — we operate as a team of builders. We execute, we build, we own, and we care deeply about our customers and their success.

What You’ll Do

  • Customer-Facing Engineering – Work closely with customers from onboarding to ongoing usage, helping them integrate and optimize our AI solutions.

  • Technical Development – Build new features, MVPs, and scalable solutions that directly impact customer outcomes.

  • Full-Stack Development – Utilize React, TypeScript, Node.js, and Python to develop robust applications and tools.

  • AI/ML Applications – Design, implement, and iterate on AI/ML solutions, including LLM prompting, tuning of voices, and transcribers to optimize use cases.

  • Integration & APIs – Manage APIs and integrations with third-party systems to ensure seamless functionality for customers.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration – Partner with Product, Engineering, and Customer Success teams to deliver tailored solutions.

  • Iterative Problem-Solving – Continuously iterate and improve AI solutions based on customer feedback and evolving requirements.

  • Project Management – Prioritize and manage multiple projects under tight deadlines while maintaining high-quality results.

Must Have

  • Strong full-stack experience: React, TypeScript, Node.js.

  • Hands-on proficiency in Python.

  • Experience building AI/ML applications, including LLM prompting and tuning.

  • Ability to manage APIs and integrate with third-party systems.

  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.

  • Proven ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects under tight deadlines.

  • Founder mindset: highly independent, takes ownership, and thrives in a fast-paced environment.

Why join us?

  • Join a world-class team of engineers and builders.

  • Backed by top investors including a16z, Y Combinator, Base10, Prysm Capital and Eurazeo.

  • Have ownership and autonomy of projects and are encouraged to ship.

  • Comprehensive Benefits including healthcare, dental, vision coverage.

  • Competitive salary + equity in a high-growth startup.

Our Operating Principles


Extreme Ownership

We take full responsibility for our work, outcomes, and team success. No excuses, no blame-shifting — if something needs fixing, we own it and make it better. This means stepping up, even when it’s not “your job.” If a ball is dropped, we pick it up. If a customer is unhappy, we fix it. If a process is broken, we redesign it. We don’t wait for someone else to solve it — we lead with accountability and expect the same from those around us.

Craftsmanship

Putting care and intention into every task, striving for excellence, and taking deep ownership of the quality and outcome of your work. Craftsmanship means never settling for “just fine.” We sweat the details because details compound. Whether it’s a product feature, an internal doc, or a sales call — we treat it as a reflection of our standards. We aim to deliver jaw-dropping customer experiences by being curious, meticulous, and proud of what we build — even when nobody’s watching.

We are “majos”
Be friendly & have fun with your coworkers. Always be genuine & honest, but kind. “Majo” is our way of saying: be a good human. Be approachable, helpful, and warm. We’re building something ambitious, and it’s easier (and more fun) when we enjoy the ride together. We give feedback with kindness, challenge each other with respect, and celebrate wins together without ego.

Urgency with Focus
Create the highest impact in the shortest amount of time. Move fast, but in the right direction. We operate with speed because time is our most limited resource. But speed without focus is chaos. We prioritize ruthlessly, act decisively, and stay aligned. We aim for high leverage: the biggest results from the simplest, smartest actions. We’re running a high-speed marathon — not a sprint with no strategy.

Talent Density and Meritocracy
Hire only people who can raise the average; ‘exceptional performance is the passing grade.’ Ability trumps seniority. We believe the best teams are built on talent density — every hire should raise the bar. We reward contribution, not titles or tenure. We give ownership to those who earn it, and we all hold each other to a high standard. A-players want to work with other A-players — that’s how we win.

First-Principles Thinking
Strip a problem to physics-level facts, ignore industry dogma, rebuild the solution from scratch. We don’t copy-paste solutions. We go back to basics, ask why things are the way they are, and rebuild from the ground up if needed. This mindset pushes us to innovate, challenge stale assumptions, and move faster than incumbents. It’s how we build what others think is impossible.

  • You’ll be working toward reducing risks from advanced AI, potentially the most important challenge of our time. raw.title: SPAR Research Manager
raw.description:
Help SPAR’s mentors become excellent research leads.

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.

 

About Kairos

Kairos is a nonprofit accelerating talent into AI safety and policy. In just over two years, we’ve trained 1,200+ people through our flagship programs:

  • SPAR: The largest AI safety research fellowship, with 800+ mentees per round mentored by researchers from Anthropic, Redwood Research, RAND, MIT, the UK AI Security Institute, and others.

  • Generator Residency: In partnership with Constellation, a platform for generalist talent to pitch, build, and ship projects that build capacity and infrastructure across the AI safety ecosystem, with advisors from OpenAI, AI Futures Project, METR, and more.

  • Global Challenges Project: A workshop series introducing promising students to careers in AI safety and biosecurity, run several times a year across Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley.

  • Pathfinder Fellowship: Helping grow the global network of AI safety university groups from a few dozen to nearly 100, with $9.5M in funding over the next two years to support their work.

We see ourselves as a portfolio of highly impactful projects in a fast-evolving field. Over the next six months, we expect to double in size and launch several new initiatives addressing critical gaps in the ecosystem.

 

The Role

SPAR is a remote, part-time fellowship that runs twice a year, with 800+ mentees, 250+ mentors, and 6,000+ applicants in the latest cohort. Many of our mentors are early-career researchers leading a team for the first time, and the quality of their mentorship shapes what hundreds of mentees learn and produce each round.

We’re looking for a Research Manager to be a mentor to our mentors. You’ll work with the researchers leading SPAR projects, helping them run their teams well, handle difficult situations, and get their work in front of the right audiences. You’ll work closely with SPAR’s program lead, and there’s room to take on broader ownership of how SPAR supports its mentors.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Support mentors across the round. You’ll be the main point of contact for a portfolio of mentors. You’ll check in with them regularly and help them scope projects, set expectations with mentees, and keep their teams on track.

  • Help first-time mentors become strong research leads. Many SPAR mentors are leading a team for the first time. You’ll coach them on running effective meetings, giving feedback, and managing mentees with very different levels of experience.

  • Handle sensitive team situations. When a team runs into conflict, a mentee stops showing up, or a mentor relationship breaks down, you’ll step in, work out what’s going on, and help everyone find a way forward.

  • Advise on research outputs. You’ll help mentors and their teams decide where and how to share their work, including which publications, workshops, and conference venues suit their results.

  • Help shape how SPAR works with mentors. You’ll contribute to how we recruit, onboard, and support mentors, and help raise the bar on research quality across the program as SPAR grows.

What you won’t do. With 250+ mentors and 800+ mentees per round, you won’t supervise individual projects in depth or co-author the research. Your impact comes from making mentors better at leading their teams, so more of their projects succeed.

 

Who You Are

  • Solid research experience. You’ve done substantial research yourself, such as a PhD, a research role, or several completed projects. You understand how research projects go well and badly, and mentors take your advice seriously.

  • Strong interpersonal judgment. You handle delicate conversations with tact, and people come to you when things are going wrong.

  • A clear communicator. You write and speak clearly, and you can give direct feedback in a way people can act on.

  • Organized. You’ll support many mentors at once during the round, often against hard deadlines. You keep careful track of commitments and follow through on them.

  • AI safety context. You’re familiar with the AI safety ecosystem and its major research agendas, and you can engage with mentors doing both technical and policy research. You don’t need to be an expert on every agenda.

  • Mission-aligned. You care about how AI development plays out, and you see SPAR as one of the most promising ways to grow the next generation of AI safety researchers.

While not required, we especially value:

  • Experience mentoring or managing junior researchers, whether in a lab, an academic group, or a research fellowship like SPAR

  • Publications at ML conferences or in AI policy venues

  • Research experience in AI safety or AI governance

 

Why Work With Us

  • You’ll be working toward reducing risks from advanced AI, potentially the most important challenge of our time. SPAR shapes who becomes an AI safety researcher and how well they learn to do research.

  • SPAR already has a strong brand, a robust mentor and mentee pipeline, and working relationships with most of the top AI safety orgs.

  • We’re building a world-class team, so you’ll be in good company. Work alongside people who’ve come to Kairos from METR, Coefficient Giving, Rethink Priorities, the UK AI Security Institute, and CEA who share your commitment to impact.

 

What We Offer

  • Salary: $105,000–$145,000 (baseline), $130,000–$180,000 (supported hubs, like London, DC, Boston, and NYC), or $145,000–$200,000 (San Francisco Bay Area), depending on experience, with potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates

  • Location: This is a remote role. We provide access to office space in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, with optional coworking elsewhere. If you work from an AI safety office in one of these cities, we cover food, lunches, and office expenses. If you work from home, we cover home office expenses.

  • Benefits: Flexible working hours, highly competitive health insurance, dental and vision coverage, generous vacation policy, and professional development budget

  • Team retreats: We host all-team retreats three times a year to connect in person, collaborate, and build team culture.

  • Travel: Work-related travel and expenses covered.

 

Logistics

  • Start date: Flexible, though we generally expect new hires to be able to start within a couple of months of applying

  • Remote, with expected travel 3–6 times a year for conferences and events, predominantly in the US

  • We’d also be happy for you to work out of any of the AI safety hubs in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston.

  • We prefer candidates who can attend meetings in the ET time zone (though our team currently spans GMT-8 to GMT+1).

  • Kairos is happy to sponsor visas to the US (typically H-1Bs or O-1As) and will likely be able to sponsor UK visas in the coming months. We can’t guarantee visa approvals, however.

 

Our Culture

We’re a small, high-trust team motivated by the urgent challenge of making advanced AI go well. We try hard to figure out where we’re wrong, which means we say uncomfortable things to each other and change our minds fairly often. We value collaborative truth-seeking, a scout mindset, agility, and an alliance mindset with the broader ecosystem.

We also believe meaningful work should be enjoyable. We support each other’s well-being, celebrate wins, and maintain a healthy sense of humor even when the work is hard.

 

Application Process

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.

  1. Application form (10–20 mins)

  2. Take-home assignment (2–4 hours, paid)

  3. Interview (45 mins)

  4. Reference checks

  5. Work trial (3 days, paid)

  6. Offer

If you’re excited about this role but unsure whether you meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re interested in multiple roles, apply to the one that best fits your skills and interests, and note in your application the other roles that you’d like to be considered for.

This role’s scope, salary, and responsibilities may evolve, and we’ll keep you in the loop about any changes if you apply.

AI tools help us review applications. If we receive more apps than we can read, some may be declined based on the AI review alone. Learn more →

raw.title: Head of Kairos Labs
raw.description:
Design, launch, and lead our incubator for new AI safety organizations.

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.


About Kairos

Kairos is a nonprofit accelerating talent into AI safety and policy. In just over two years, we’ve trained 1,200+ people through our flagship programs:

  • SPAR: The largest AI safety research fellowship, with 800+ mentees per round mentored by researchers from Anthropic, Redwood Research, RAND, MIT, the UK AI Security Institute, and others.

  • Generator Residency: In partnership with Constellation, a platform for generalist talent to pitch, build, and ship projects that build capacity and infrastructure across the AI safety ecosystem, with advisors from OpenAI, AI Futures Project, METR, and more.

  • Global Challenges Project: A workshop series introducing promising students to careers in AI safety and biosecurity, run several times a year across Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley.

  • Pathfinder Fellowship: Helping grow the global network of AI safety university groups from a few dozen to nearly 100, with $9.5M in funding over the next two years to support their work.

We see ourselves as a portfolio of highly impactful projects in a fast-evolving field. Over the next six months, we expect to double in size and launch several new initiatives addressing critical gaps in the ecosystem.

 

The Role

We’re looking for a founding Head of Kairos Labs to design, launch, and lead Kairos Labs, our upcoming incubator for new AI safety projects and organizations. Kairos Labs will help founders take promising ideas from concept to independent organization, with hands-on advising and operational support. Where our Generator Residency gives generalists a platform to build projects within the ecosystem, Kairos Labs is aimed at people setting out to start something new.

Kairos Labs is at an early stage, and it’s one of the biggest bets we’re making with our new funding. The program is fully funded for its first two years, but most decisions about its shape haven’t been made yet, so you’d be building the program from the ground up. We hope to design it in late 2026 and launch in early 2027.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Design the program. The plan is an incubator for new AI safety organizations, but there are still many open questions. You’ll help decide which kinds of organizations we take on, whether projects join in cohorts or on a rolling basis, how long they stay, what support they get, and when they’re ready to operate on their own.

  • Own the launch. You’ll build the application and selection process, recruit the first projects, and set up the program’s operations.

  • Support incubated projects. You’ll be the main advisor to Kairos Labs founders, helping them with strategy, fundraising, and hiring, and making sure their operational needs are met.

  • Own Kairos Labs’ strategic direction. You’ll decide how the program grows, including how many projects to take on, what kinds of organizations the ecosystem most needs, and how Kairos Labs relates to our other programs.

  • Contribute to Kairos more broadly. As bandwidth allows, you’ll help shape org-wide strategy, weigh in on new programs, and participate in cross-cutting work.

 

Who You Are

  • Experience building organizations. You’ve founded something yourself, or run a comparable incubator, accelerator, fellowship, or fiscal-sponsorship program, and you’ve seen firsthand what early-stage organizations need.

  • AI safety context. Kairos Labs’ theory of change depends on a clear picture of what the ecosystem is missing. You should have views on which organizations are worth starting, which gaps matter most, and who is positioned to fill them.

  • Strong judgment about projects and people. You’ll make calls about which founders to back and which ideas are worth turning into organizations, often with limited evidence.

  • High agency. Because you’re owning Kairos Labs from the beginning, you should be comfortable building a vision from scratch, executing on it autonomously, and answering big open questions about the program as they come up.

  • Mission-aligned. You care deeply about making advanced AI go well, and you believe getting new AI safety organizations off the ground is one of the most promising ways to help.

  • Operationally fluent. Incubating organizations comes with serious legal, financial, and compliance work, likely including fiscal sponsorship. You don’t need to be a lawyer or accountant, but you should be comfortable handling that side of the work with expert help.

 

Why Work With Us

  • You’ll be working toward reducing risks from advanced AI, potentially the most important challenge of our time. Kairos Labs will shape which new organizations get built in AI safety. If you do this well, several new AI safety organizations will exist because of you.

  • You’ll get to design and own the program from scratch, with the backing of an established, funded organization.

  • We’re building a world-class team, so you’ll be in good company. Work alongside people who’ve come to Kairos from METR, Coefficient Giving, Rethink Priorities, the UK AI Security Institute, and CEA who share your commitment to impact.

  • Collaborate regularly with leading AI safety researchers, policy professionals, funders, and organizers.

 

What We Offer

  • Salary: $140,000–$195,000 (baseline), $175,000–$245,000 (supported hubs, like London, DC, Boston, and NYC), or $195,000–$270,000 (San Francisco Bay Area), depending on experience, with potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates

  • Location: This is a remote role. We provide access to office space in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, with optional coworking elsewhere. If you work from an AI safety office in one of these cities, we cover food, lunches, and office expenses. If you work from home, we cover home office expenses.

  • Benefits: Flexible working hours, highly competitive health insurance, dental and vision coverage, generous vacation policy, and professional development budget

  • Team retreats: We host all-team retreats three times a year to connect in person, collaborate, and build team culture.

  • Travel: Work-related travel and expenses covered.

 

Logistics

  • Start date: Ideally by October or early November 2026, ahead of the program design push in December and a planned launch in early 2027

  • Remote, with expected travel 3–6 times a year for conferences and events, predominantly in the US

  • We’d also be happy for you to work out of any of the AI safety hubs in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston.

  • We prefer candidates who can attend meetings in the ET time zone (though our team currently spans GMT-8 to GMT+1).

  • Kairos is happy to sponsor visas to the US (typically H-1Bs or O-1As) and will likely be able to sponsor UK visas in the coming months. We can’t guarantee visa approvals, however.

 

Our Culture

We’re a small, high-trust team motivated by the urgent challenge of making advanced AI go well. We try hard to figure out where we’re wrong, which means we say uncomfortable things to each other and change our minds fairly often. We value collaborative truth-seeking, a scout mindset, agility, and an alliance mindset with the broader ecosystem.

We also believe meaningful work should be enjoyable. We support each other’s well-being, celebrate wins, and maintain a healthy sense of humor even when the work is hard.

 

Application Process

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.

  1. Application form (10–20 mins)

  2. Take-home assignment (2–4 hours, paid)

  3. Interview (45 mins)

  4. Reference checks

  5. Work trial (3 days, paid)

  6. Offer

If you’re excited about this role but unsure whether you meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re interested in multiple roles, apply to the one that best fits your skills and interests, and note in your application the other roles that you’d like to be considered for.

This role’s scope, salary, and responsibilities may evolve, and we’ll keep you in the loop about any changes if you apply.

AI tools help us review applications. If we receive more apps than we can read, some may be declined based on the AI review alone. Learn more →

raw.title: Generalist (Groups)
raw.description:
Join Kairos’s university groups team to support AI safety group organizers through the Pathfinder Fellowship and shape what Kairos does for university groups next.

Depending on experience, we consider candidates for the Generalist (Groups) or Senior Generalist (Groups) version of this role.

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.

 

About Kairos

Kairos is a nonprofit accelerating talent into AI safety and policy. In just over two years, we’ve trained 1,200+ people through our flagship programs:

  • SPAR: The largest AI safety research fellowship, with 800+ mentees per round mentored by researchers from Anthropic, Redwood Research, RAND, MIT, the UK AI Security Institute, and others.

  • Generator Residency: In partnership with Constellation, a platform for generalist talent to pitch, build, and ship projects that build capacity and infrastructure across the AI safety ecosystem, with advisors from OpenAI, AI Futures Project, METR, and more.

  • Global Challenges Project: A workshop series introducing promising students to careers in AI safety and biosecurity, run several times a year across Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley.

  • Pathfinder Fellowship: Helping grow the global network of AI safety university groups from a few dozen to nearly 100, with $9.5M in funding over the next two years to support their work.

We see ourselves as a portfolio of highly impactful projects in a fast-evolving field. Over the next six months, we expect to double in size and launch several new initiatives addressing critical gaps in the ecosystem.

 

The Role

University groups are where many people first get involved in AI safety, and Kairos runs some of the ecosystem’s core infrastructure for them. Through the Pathfinder Fellowship, we provide mentorship and funding to organizers of AI safety university groups around the world, and through OASIS we bring top organizers together for in-person workshops. Over the past year, this work has grown from a fraction of our time to one of our core priorities, and we’re now growing the team behind it.

We’re looking for a generalist to work across the whole area, including helping run the Pathfinder Fellowship, organizing in-person events, seeding new groups at universities we’re not yet reaching, and helping strong organizers transition into full-time work in AI safety. The exact shape of the role will evolve with your strengths and where we most need capacity.

We’re also weighing more ambitious bets for the program, like hiring full-time organizers at top groups, funding ambitious student-run events (symposiums, summer intensives), experimenting with radically different group formats, overhauling our organizer resource center, and giving the strongest groups much more hands-on support. You’d help shape which of these we pursue.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Help run the Pathfinder Fellowship. You’ll help onboard new groups and organizers, coordinate mentorship, handle communications with organizers and mentors, and process the grants that fund groups’ work.

  • Help run in-person events. You’ll support the planning and logistics of OASIS, our workshop for top organizers at Constellation in Berkeley, and other events for organizers and students.

  • Seed new groups. You’ll find and support founders at strong universities that don’t yet have an AI safety group.

  • Help organizers go full-time. You’ll support the strongest organizers in moving into full-time work in AI safety, whether that’s continuing to organize or heading into research, policy, or operations.

  • Build the systems behind the program. You’ll improve the infrastructure the Pathfinder Fellowship runs on (applications, grants, communications) and automate the work that shouldn’t be done by hand.

  • Pitch in on broader Kairos work as capacity allows. You’ll help on active programs like SPAR, Generator, and the Global Challenges Project, build relationships across the AI safety ecosystem, and ship small cross-team projects.

 

Who You Are

  • A past university AI safety group organizer. You’ve started or helped run an AI safety university group, and you know what organizers need because you’ve been one.

  • Mission-aligned with context on AI safety. You care deeply about making advanced AI go well, and you have enough context on the ecosystem to make good judgments about which groups and organizers are promising and where to focus our support.

  • High agency and able to figure things out. Much of this work won’t have a playbook. You’ll be designing processes as you run them and adjusting our approach as we learn what works.

  • People-oriented. Most of the role is supporting organizers. You should be someone they enjoy working with, trust with hard questions, and come to when they’re stuck.

  • Organized and on top of things. You keep careful track of to-dos and information. When you drop a ball, it’s on purpose.

  • Strong writer and communicator. You’re clear and concise, and you think through your messaging from the reader’s perspective.

 

While not required, we especially value:

  • Familiarity with Kairos’s university groups programs (for example, as a participant in the Pathfinder Fellowship or OASIS)

  • Experience with event planning or community building

  • A track record of starting and shipping things independently

 

Why Work With Us

  • You’ll be working toward reducing risks from advanced AI, potentially the most important challenge of our time. The groups you support are where many future AI safety and policy professionals get their start.

  • University groups are a central part of Kairos’s strategy over the coming years, and you’d be joining the small team shaping how we scale that work.

  • You’ll get to shape the role around your interests, with a say in which parts of the university groups portfolio you take on.

  • We’re building a world-class team, so you’ll be in good company. Work alongside people who’ve come to Kairos from METR, Coefficient Giving, Rethink Priorities, the UK AI Security Institute, and CEA who share your commitment to impact.

  • Collaborate regularly with leading AI safety researchers, policy professionals, funders, and organizers.

 

What We Offer

  • Salary: $105,000–$145,000 (baseline), $130,000–$180,000 (supported hubs, like London, DC, Boston, and NYC), or $145,000–$200,000 (San Francisco Bay Area), depending on experience, with potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates

  • Location: This is a remote role. We provide access to office space in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, with optional coworking elsewhere. If you work from an AI safety office in one of these cities, we cover food, lunches, and office expenses. If you work from home, we cover home office expenses.

  • Benefits: Flexible working hours, highly competitive health insurance, dental and vision coverage, generous vacation policy, and professional development budget

  • Team retreats: We host all-team retreats three times a year to connect in person, collaborate, and build team culture.

  • Travel: Work-related travel and expenses covered.

 

Logistics

  • Start date: Ideally by October or early November 2026, with flexibility for the right candidate

  • Remote, with expected travel 3–6 times a year for conferences and events, predominantly in the US

  • We’d also be happy for you to work out of any of the AI safety hubs in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston.

  • We prefer candidates who can attend meetings in the ET time zone (though our team currently spans GMT-8 to GMT+1).

  • Kairos is happy to sponsor visas to the US (typically H-1Bs or O-1As) and will likely be able to sponsor UK visas in the coming months. We can’t guarantee visa approvals, however.

 

Our Culture

We’re a small, high-trust team motivated by the urgent challenge of making advanced AI go well. We try hard to figure out where we’re wrong, which means we say uncomfortable things to each other and change our minds fairly often. We value collaborative truth-seeking, a scout mindset, agility, and an alliance mindset with the broader ecosystem.

We also believe meaningful work should be enjoyable. We support each other’s well-being, celebrate wins, and maintain a healthy sense of humor even when the work is hard.

 

Application Process

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.

  1. Application form (10–20 mins)

  2. Take-home assignment (2–4 hours, paid)

  3. Interview (45 mins)

  4. Reference checks

  5. Work trial (3 days, paid)

  6. Offer

If you’re excited about this role but unsure whether you meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re interested in multiple roles, apply to the one that best fits your skills and interests, and note in your application the other roles that you’d like to be considered for.

This role’s scope, salary, and responsibilities may evolve, and we’ll keep you in the loop about any changes if you apply.

raw.title: Head of Special Projects
raw.description:
Lead a new team with a broad mandate to pursue high-impact opportunities for the AI safety ecosystem, including one-off projects and Kairos’s next programs.

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.


About Kairos

Kairos is a nonprofit accelerating talent into AI safety and policy. In just over two years, we’ve trained 1,200+ people through our flagship programs:

  • SPAR: The largest AI safety research fellowship, with 800+ mentees per round mentored by researchers from Anthropic, Redwood Research, RAND, MIT, the UK AI Security Institute, and others.

  • Generator Residency: In partnership with Constellation, a platform for generalist talent to pitch, build, and ship projects that build capacity and infrastructure across the AI safety ecosystem, with advisors from OpenAI, AI Futures Project, METR, and more.

  • Global Challenges Project: A workshop series introducing promising students to careers in AI safety and biosecurity, run several times a year across Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley.

  • Pathfinder Fellowship: Helping grow the global network of AI safety university groups from a few dozen to nearly 100, with $9.5M in funding over the next two years to support their work.

We see ourselves as a portfolio of highly impactful projects in a fast-evolving field. Over the next six months, we expect to double in size and launch several new initiatives addressing critical gaps in the ecosystem.

 

The Role

Kairos has historically made a small number of large, ongoing bets, like SPAR and Pathfinder. Running Generator taught us that this left a lot of value on the table. A surprising number of time-bound opportunities are worth pursuing, whether that’s an event, a one-off program, or a project that responds to a narrow window for impact, even when they don’t have a clean home elsewhere in the ecosystem. We’re starting a Special Projects team to go after them.

The team has a broad mandate and a large initial budget. You’d pursue high-impact opportunities as we find them, in talent work and beyond, running small and medium-sized projects that respond to what the ecosystem needs right now. Some will be short-lived by design. Others may prove out an idea that becomes a lasting Kairos program. Generator went from an idea to a 27-resident cohort at Constellation in a matter of months, and Talent Commons, our shared talent database, will likely become a core part of how Kairos, and much of the AI safety ecosystem, routes talent. It’d be up to you which projects you take on, and we expect many of the best ones to be ideas we haven’t had yet.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Own a small portfolio of early-stage bets. You’ll run one to three new projects at a time, taking each from concept to something operating in the world.

  • Decide what we pursue. You’ll evaluate opportunities from across the team and the ecosystem, including your own ideas, make the case for which ones are worth attempting, and move fast when a window is closing.

  • Scale what works, wind down what doesn’t. When a pilot succeeds, you’ll build the systems it needs to run reliably, then keep owning it or hand it to a long-term owner. When a project has run its course, you’ll close it out cleanly and carry the lessons into the next one.

  • Grow the team around the work. As projects mature, you’ll likely hire people to run them and manage them as a small team.

  • Contribute to Kairos more broadly. As bandwidth allows, you’ll help shape org-wide strategy, weigh in on new programs, and participate in cross-cutting work.

 

Who You Are

  • Experience starting things. You’ve taken a program, an organization, a product, or a community from an idea to something up and running.

  • Quick to execute. Many of these opportunities are time-bound. You’re comfortable shipping in weeks rather than quarters and making calls with incomplete information.

  • AI safety context. Choosing which bets deserve Kairos’s time requires a clear picture of what the ecosystem is missing. You should come with views of your own about what’s worth building.

  • Comfortable with an evolving mandate. Your portfolio will change under you as projects launch, hand off, or wind down, and you should be happy working that way.

  • Mission-aligned. You care deeply about reducing risks from advanced AI, and you see new programs like these as one of the most promising ways to fill the ecosystem’s gaps.

 

Why Work With Us

  • You’ll be working toward reducing risks from advanced AI, potentially the most important challenge of our time. The projects you start could become Kairos’s next core programs and address critical bottlenecks in AI safety.

  • Few roles offer this much room to decide what you work on. You’ll shape the portfolio, and with it a meaningful part of Kairos’s direction.

  • We’re building a world-class team, so you’ll be in good company. Work alongside people who’ve come to Kairos from METR, Coefficient Giving, Rethink Priorities, the UK AI Security Institute, and CEA who share your commitment to impact.

  • Collaborate regularly with leading AI safety researchers, policy professionals, funders, and organizers.

 

What We Offer

  • Salary: $140,000–$195,000 (baseline), $175,000–$245,000 (supported hubs, like London, DC, Boston, and NYC), or $195,000–$270,000 (San Francisco Bay Area), depending on experience, with potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates

  • Location: This is a remote role. We provide access to office space in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, with optional coworking elsewhere. If you work from an AI safety office in one of these cities, we cover food, lunches, and office expenses. If you work from home, we cover home office expenses.

  • Benefits: Flexible working hours, highly competitive health insurance, dental and vision coverage, generous vacation policy, and professional development budget

  • Team retreats: We host all-team retreats three times a year to connect in person, collaborate, and build team culture.

  • Travel: Work-related travel and expenses covered.

 

Logistics

  • Start date: Flexible, though we generally expect new hires to be able to start within a couple of months of applying

  • Remote, with expected travel 3–6 times a year for conferences and events, predominantly in the US

  • We’d also be happy for you to work out of any of the AI safety hubs in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston.

  • We prefer candidates who can attend meetings in the ET time zone (though our team currently spans GMT-8 to GMT+1).

  • Kairos is happy to sponsor visas to the US (typically H-1Bs or O-1As) and will likely be able to sponsor UK visas in the coming months. We can’t guarantee visa approvals, however.

 

Our Culture

We’re a small, high-trust team motivated by the urgent challenge of making advanced AI go well. We try hard to figure out where we’re wrong, which means we say uncomfortable things to each other and change our minds fairly often. We value collaborative truth-seeking, a scout mindset, agility, and an alliance mindset with the broader ecosystem.

We also believe meaningful work should be enjoyable. We support each other’s well-being, celebrate wins, and maintain a healthy sense of humor even when the work is hard.

 

Application Process

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.

  1. Application form (10–20 mins)

  2. Take-home assignment (2–4 hours, paid)

  3. Interview (45 mins)

  4. Reference checks

  5. Work trial (3 days, paid)

  6. Offer

If you’re excited about this role but unsure whether you meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re interested in multiple roles, apply to the one that best fits your skills and interests, and note in your application the other roles that you’d like to be considered for.

This role’s scope, salary, and responsibilities may evolve, and we’ll keep you in the loop about any changes if you apply.

AI tools help us review applications. If we receive more apps than we can read, some may be declined based on the AI review alone. Learn more →

 

Questions? Reach out at Know someone who might be a good fit? If your referral gets hired and completes two months with us, we’ll pay you a $10,000 referral bonus. Learn more here.

Wir setzen auf Umsetzung und entwickeln konkrete, smarte Lösungen, indem wir Wärmepumpen, Batteriespeicher und Smart Metering einfach zugänglich, zuverlässig und bezahlbar machen. Wir sind ein profitables Greentech-Startup und glauben, dass nachhaltiger Impact und langfristiges Wachstum nur auf Basis eines gesunden Geschäftsmodells möglich sind. Um unsere ambitionierte Tech Roadmap umzusetzen haben wir im Frühjahr 2026 eine Seed-Finanzierung in Höhe von 10 Millionen Euro mit Set Ventures und AENU abgeschlossen. Getrieben von Kundennutzen, Klarheit und Verantwortung stehen wir für hochwertige Heizlösungen und ein Arbeitsumfeld, in dem Menschen Verantwortung übernehmen und nachhaltigen Mehrwert schaffen. Als Founders Associate CEO Office (m/w/d) bei GALVANY arbeitest du im CEO-Office direkt mit unserem Gründer Raik und dem Leadership-Team zusammen. Du treibst strategische und operative Themen quer durch das Unternehmen. Du wirst Teil eines Teams, das Erfahrungen aus Top-Strategieberatungen (MBB), Unicorns und Private Equity mitbringt und von führenden Universitäten wie TUM, INSEAD und Berkeley kommt. Deine Aufgaben GTM: Du treibst Growth-Initiativen in einem schnell wachsenden Start-up voran, entwickelst datenbasierte Go-to-Market-Strategien und setzt diese um– von der ersten Marktanalyse bis zum Launch neuer Produkte mit ersten Partnern. Cross-funktionale Zusammenarbeit: Du arbeitest eng mit Sales, Marketing, Product und Customer Success zusammen, um die Customer Journey abteilungsübergreifend zu koordinieren, Reibungsverluste zu minimieren und eine gemeinsame Strategie umzusetzen. Prozessaufbau & -optimierung: Du baust Prozesse von Grund auf, dokumentierst sie sauber und entwickelst sie kontinuierlich weiter. Du denkst in Strukturen, erkennst Ineffizienzen früh und setzt Verbesserungen hands-on um. Research & strategische Analyse: Du führst eigenständig Markt-, Wettbewerbs- und Potenzialanalysen durch, leitest konkrete Handlungsempfehlungen ab und bereitest Ergebnisse für das Leadership-Team auf. Strategische Partnerschaften: Du identifizierst relevante Partner, bereitest Erstgespräche vor, unterstützt bei der Entwicklung von Value Propositions und begleitest den Aufbau strategischer Kooperationen von der Ansprache bis zur Vereinbarung. AI & Automation: Du identifizierst Automatisierungspotenziale in internen Prozessen und Geschäftsmodellen, testest KI-Tools und -Workflows und trägst aktiv dazu bei, wie Galvany künstliche Intelligenz operativ einsetzt – zur Effizienzsteigerung, Produktentwicklung und Entscheidungsfindung. Dein Profil Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Master Studium an einer Top-Universität in einem wirtschaftswissenschaftlichen Studiengang. Du hast erste praktische Erfahrungen in einem dynamischen Umfeld gesammelt z. B. in einem Start-up, einer Unternehmensberatung oder einem VC. Du denkst strukturiert, analytisch und zahlenaffin und kannst komplexe Sachverhalte schnell durchdringen, sauber aufbereiten und klar kommunizieren. Du trittst sicher auf und überzeugst unterschiedliche Stakeholder, intern wie extern, durch präzise, verständliche Kommunikation, auch in anspruchsvollen Situationen. Du arbeitest selbstständig, bringst Themen eigenverantwortlich voran und verlierst auch in einem schnellen, sich verändernden Umfeld nicht den Überblick. Du bist neugierig auf KI-Tools und Automatisierung und hast idealerweise bereits erste Erfahrungen damit gesammelt oder den Willen, dich schnell einzuarbeiten. Du verfügst über sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift. Zusätzlich sind uns folgende Fähigkeiten und Eigenschaften wichtig: Entrepreneurial Mindset: Du übernimmst Verantwortung, handelst proaktiv und machst aus Unklarheit eine Chance. Du verbindest Kreativität mit einem Macher-Mindset, um Dinge voranzubringen. Methodical: Du denkst und arbeitest geordnet, klar und nachvollziehbar – in deinen Gedankengängen genauso wie in der Art, wie du Informationen aufbereitest und präsentierst. Strategic Thinker: Du planst über den nächsten Monat hinaus, erkennst frühzeitig, was das Team in 6–12 Monaten braucht, und bringst die richtigen Initiativen auf den Weg. Clear Communicator: Du kannst komplexe Themen für unterschiedliche Zielgruppen verständlich aufbereiten – schriftlich wie mündlich – und bleibst auch in schwierigen Situationen sachlich und klar. Collaborative: Du arbeitest eng mit verschiedenen Teams zusammen – von Sales über Marketing bis hin zu Operations – um Botschaften und Strategie aufeinander abzustimmen. Benefits Werde Teil eines schnell wachsenden und profitablen Climate-Tech-Startups Attraktive und wettbewerbsfähige Vergütung Unser lebendiges Office ist das Herz unserer Kultur und fördert Zusammenarbeit und Austausch vor Ort Individuelle Benefits, abgestimmt auf deine Bedürfnisse, z. title: General Manager (m/w/d) - Fitness & Lifestyle Brand
description: Managing Director (m/w/d) - Fitness & Lifestyle Brand Location: Köln Start: Ab sofort Setup: Vollzeit (on-site) THE BRAND & THE OPPORTUNITY Du baust gemeinsam mit uns eine neue Fitness-Marke im Segment Mid Cost - High Value auf. Die Vision: „ Der neue Hotspot in der City für Workout, Recovery, Co-Working und Socializing.“ Kraft, Cardio und Functional, Live-Kurse, Sauna und Recovery, Bar und Lounge sowie eine ruhige Co-Working Zone, alles unter einem Dach - zu einem erschwinglichen Preis deutlich unter Premium-Clubs. Unsere Clubs sollen auf ehemaligen Retail-Flächen entstehen, in 1A-Innenstadtlagen mit langfristig gesicherten Mietverträgen. Wir starten in Westdeutschland in der Region Köln, Essen, Frankfurt und expandieren dann. Wir arbeiten mit unternehmerischem Anspruch: kleines Team, kurze Wege, jeder Standort muss sich selbst tragen. Der erste Club ist der Beweis für das Konzept, und jeder weitere wird durch den Erfolg des vorherigen verdient. Für dich heißt das: Du bist ab Sekunde 1 dabei und gestaltest vom Namen über das Konzept bis hin zur Location alles von Grund auf mit. Kein Einstieg in einen bestehenden Betrieb, sondern die Chance, eine Marke von Null an aufzubauen , das Modell in allen Details zu gestalten und volle Verantwortung für das Ergebnis zu übernehmen. THE ROLE & YOUR ROADMAP Als Managing Director verantwortest du den kompletten Aufbau der Marke - von den ersten Entwürfen auf dem Reißbrett bis hin zur Multi-Site-Skalierung. Phase 1 - Konzept schärfen: Du bringst das Angebot, das Flächenprogramm, die Pricing-Strategie und den Brand-Auftritt gemeinsam mit den Gesellschaftern zur Marktreife. Phase 2 - Ersten Club eröffnen: Du steuerst den Ausbau vor Ort, baust dein Kernteam auf, drehst den Pre-Opening-Sales auf Anschlag und bringst den ersten Flagship-Standort ans Netz. Phase 3 - Proof of Concept: Du erreichst mit dem Club die geplanten Mitglieder- und Ergebniszahlen (P&L) und machst aus dem Piloten ein hocheffizientes, wiederholbares Modell. Phase 4 - Skalieren: Du eröffnest weitere Standorte in Deutschland und baust die Organisation auf, die dieses Wachstum trägt. YOUR IMPACT (DIE ERSTEN 12 MONATE) Du bist von Tag 1 an am Start und bringst den ersten Standort ans Netz: Konzept zur Marktreife bringen: Zusammen mit der Projektleitung feilst du an Angebot, Flächenaufteilung, Preisen und Marke. Ausbau steuern: Du betreust den Aus- und Umbau des ersten Standorts und behältst Zeit- und Kostenrahmen fest im Griff. Kernteam aufbauen: Du rekrutierst Club-Leitung, Trainer sowie Servicepersonal und prägst von Anfang an Kultur und Standards. Pre-Sales & Markteintritt verantworten: Du treibst die Mitgliedergewinnung vor der Eröffnung, machst lokales Marketing und schließt Deals mit Firmenkunden sowie Aggregatoren (z. B. Urban Sports Club, EGYM Wellpass). Prozesse & Tech aufsetzen: Du richtest Mitgliederverwaltung, Zugangssysteme, App und Reporting ein. Ersten Club eröffnen: Du begleitest das Grand Opening und führst den Standort erfolgreich in den Live-Betrieb. YOUR PROFILE Du brennst selbst für Fitness und Lifestyle, denkst wie ein Unternehmer und hast den Biss, etwas Eigenes aufzubauen? Dann bist du genau die richtige Person! Track Record: Du hast Führungserfahrung in der Fitnessbranche (z. B. als Area Manager, Cluster Manager oder Regional Director), idealerweise mit P&L Verantwortung. Neueröffnungs-Erfahrung: Du hast schon eine Neueröffnung von A bis Z selbst verantwortet oder mitgestaltet (Ausbau, Teamaufbau, Pre-Sales). Business Mindset: Du hast Kaufmännisches Denken, Data-Drive und souveränes Auftreten gegenüber Gesellschaftern, Vermietern und Partnern. Hands-on & Drive: Du packst überall mit an, bis du zufrieden bist. Danach führst du ein wachsendes Team. Setup: Vollzeit, Wohnsitz oder Relocation in die Startregion Köln, Essen oder Frankfurt. Reisebereitschaft zu den Standorten und Deutsch C2. Das wäre ein Plus: Vorerfahrung aus Hospitality, Wellness oder Gastronomie, Erfahrung im Markenaufbau sowie ein starkes Netzwerk in der Fitnessbranche. WHY US Maximale Gestaltungsfreiheit: Die seltene Chance, eine komplett neue Marke von der ersten Skizze an zu ownen. High-Speed & Support: Kurze Entscheidungswege und direkter Austausch mit den Gesellschaftern. Du entscheidest alles mit! Executive Package: Attraktive Vergütung bestehend aus Fixgehalt, transparentem Bonus und einem Firmenwagen. Contact: Alex Berwanger Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Datacentre Deployment Lead
description: <p></p> <p><strong>ABOUT NEXGEN CLOUD</strong></p> <p>NexGen Cloud is a fast-growing GPU cloud and AI infrastructure business. We're the company behind Hyperstack — a self-serve, on-demand cloud platform built for high-performance AI, HPC, and compute-heavy workloads. Powered by 100% renewable energy and NVIDIA architecture, Hyperstack gives teams from AI startups to enterprise the compute they need, without the cost or complexity of legacy cloud.</p> <p>We move fast, solve hard problems, and build things that matter. If you want ownership, real impact, and a front-row seat to one of the most consequential infrastructure shifts of the decade — this is the place.</p> <p><strong>THE ROLE: DATA CENTRE DEPLOYMENT LEAD</strong></p> <p>We're building GPU clusters across multiple international regions, and none of that capacity reaches customers until it's racked, cabled, commissioned and handed over. Our Senior Deployment Lead owns the pipeline but can't be on every site at once, so we need a senior onsite authority who can lead each build and hold every region to the same standard.</p> <p>This is a role for someone who's happiest on the data centre floor making the call, not waiting for one. You'll lead a team of 3–5 Deployment Engineers through each build, catch problems at planning before hardware lands, and hand over sites that Operations can run from day two. Expect around 50% international travel, remote-first in between.</p> <p><strong>WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING</strong></p> <p>Rather than a checklist, here's what success in this role actually looks like:</p> <ul> <li>Own each site as the onsite decision-maker, leading Deployment Engineers day to day, directing contractors safely, and escalating only what genuinely sits beyond onsite authority.</li> <li>Collaborate closely with the Senior Deployment Lead, Network Engineering, Procurement &amp; Supply Chain, and Data Centre Operations/NOC to take every build from validated design to clean handover.</li> <li>Validate design plans and BOMs before hardware arrives, checking space, power, cooling, weight and interoperability (optics, AOC, DAC) so issues are fixed at planning, not on site.</li> <li>Produce and validate structured and fibre cabling designs, including length estimates, oversee cable pathing, and run cabling QC so every install matches the design before sign-off.</li> <li>Oversee racking and installation of GPU servers and network hardware, support fabric installation and cutover, and make sure commissioning meets the agreed acceptance criteria.</li> <li>Define and enforce the deployment standards every region builds to — rack, cabling, labelling and documentation — and hand over every site with complete as-built records.</li> <li>Run post-deployment reviews, turn the findings into better workflows, and develop your engineers so the team takes on more of each build over time.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ABOUT YOU</strong></p> <p>We care more about how you think and work than a perfect CV. You'll likely bring a combination of the following:</p> <p><em>Essential:</em></p> <ul> <li>Experience leading a technical deployment team on site — allocating work and acting as the onsite authority, not just the most experienced engineer on the crew.</li> <li>Advanced structured and fibre cabling experience, including producing designs, estimating lengths and running QC.</li> <li>Experience creating and reviewing BOMs against space, power, cooling, weight and interoperability, including optics, AOC and DAC.</li> <li>Significant data centre deployment experience, with strong network and server hardware knowledge, and a track record of writing or enforcing standards and documentation others followed.</li> <li>Willingness to travel internationally around 50% of the time (sometimes at short notice, for days or weeks at a time), and fluent English with clear written reporting.</li> </ul> <p><em>Nice to Have:</em></p> <ul> <li>GPU or HPC cluster build experience, ideally including InfiniBand and fat-tree or rail-optimised fabric designs.</li> <li>Experience leading a multi-person deployment team across more than one country.</li> <li>Scripting experience, for example Python.</li> </ul> <p><strong>WHAT WE OFFER</strong></p> <ul> <li>Competitive salary and annual discretionary bonus scheme</li> <li>Employee wellbeing benefits</li> <li>25 days holiday, plus public holidays</li> <li>Private Medical Insurance</li> <li>Enhanced Pension Scheme</li> <li>Remote-first working, with international travel to our deployment sites</li> <li>Real ownership and autonomy — the trust to take initiative and experiment</li> <li>Visible, meaningful impact as we scale</li> <li>Clear career progression in a high-growth company</li> <li>A collaborative, international culture built on trust, transparency, and ownership</li> <li>The chance to help shape NexGen Cloud's team, culture, and future</li> </ul> <p><strong>WHY APPLY</strong></p> <p>We welcome applications from all backgrounds. If you enjoy solving complex infrastructure problems and want to build something meaningful at scale, we'd like to hear from you.</p> <p><strong>MORE INFORMATION</strong></p> <p>Visit our <a href="https://www.nexgencloud.com/careers">careers page</a> to learn more about us or follow us on <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/nexgen-cloud">LinkedIn</a> and <a href="https://x.com/CloudNexgen">X</a> to learn more about our journey and keep up with our latest news and releases.</p> <p></p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Product Manager, Consumer - Audiobooks
description: We're looking for a strategic, detail-oriented Senior Product Manager to join the Books Vertical and lead end-to-end book experiences on Spotify: from discovery and conversion through to listening, and from the creator pipeline through to the consumer shelf. This role is about connecting the dots across our core experiences, conversion flows, content pipeline, and creator tooling to make books work seamlessly on Spotify. Books are a major focus for Spotify, and we need someone who can look holistically across the book ecosystem to identify gaps, reduce friction, and make sure our experiences are coherent end-to-end. You'll focus on making the full books journey work better for listeners, creators, and rights-holders, not just shipping new features. You'll partner closely with Personalization, Subscriptions, Experience, and creator-facing teams to strengthen and evolve book experiences across surfaces, and help shape a product strategy that directly improves how listeners discover and enjoy books. What You'll Do Shape and execute product strategy across core book experiences, conversion flows, content pipeline, and creator tooling. Partner with teams across Spotify to identify and close gaps across book surfaces, creating a coherent end-to-end experience from content pipeline through to the consumer experience. Collaborate with Design, Engineering, Product Insights, and Program Management to lead improvements across discovery, conversion, listening, and creator-facing surfaces. Conduct, commission, and use research to understand listener behavior, creator needs, book consumption patterns, and market trends. Use qualitative and quantitative insights to identify the most impactful opportunities across the book ecosystem and prioritize accordingly. Define and track success metrics across the book experience, connecting upstream pipeline health with downstream listener outcomes. Identify systemic friction points and opportunities across the book ecosystem, and advocate for improvements that strengthen the end-to-end experience. Who You Are You have 4+ years of experience in product management, ideally working across complex product ecosystems with multiple surfaces, partners, and dependencies. You have a track record of improving multi-surface product experiences, not just launching new features but making existing systems work better together. You use analytics, A/B testing, and user research to guide product decisions. You're comfortable working across both consumer-facing and platform or tooling surfaces, and can move between listener needs and creator needs. You communicate clearly and build shared understanding across teams that don't always see each other's work, translating between consumer, pipeline, and creator perspectives. You're comfortable with ambiguity and managing complexity across multiple teams and partners. You think in systems and map how changes in one part of the ecosystem (content pipeline, creator tooling, conversion flows, consumer surfaces) affect the rest. You look for the most impactful fix rather than optimizing surfaces in isolation. Where You'll Be This role is based in London or Stockholm We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home. Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! As an Applied Research Engineer in our Video team, you will help build the next generation of production-grade foundation models for human-centric video generation.

You will join a highly focused team working at the intersection of large-scale generative modeling, distributed systems, and production engineering. Our mission is to develop and optimize video base models that power realistic, controllable, and emotionally expressive synthetic humans at scale.

This is not pure research. This is applied research with direct product impact.

You will work on advancing training recipes, scaling distributed systems, improving evaluation frameworks, and optimizing inference to ensure our models are high quality, stable, and efficient enough for real-world deployment. Your work will directly influence models used by tens of thousands of businesses worldwide.

What you’ll do

You will own and execute end-to-end research and engineering projects, from hypothesis to production impact. This includes:

  • Developing and scaling latent video diffusion models tailored for human-centric video generation

  • Advancing distributed training strategies (DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed, sequence parallelism) under real compute constraints

  • Improving training stability at multi-node scale

  • Designing rigorous evaluation frameworks combining automated metrics and structured human evaluation

  • Optimizing inference for low latency, high resolution, and cost efficiency

  • Running controlled ablations and experiments to drive high-signal modeling decisions

  • Contributing to high engineering standards: reproducibility, experiment tracking, CI/CD, monitoring

You will be expected to move fast, run multiple hypotheses in parallel, identify signal early, and focus on outcomes rather than exploration for its own sake.

  • Strong experience training deep learning models at scale

  • Strong Python and PyTorch skills

  • Hands-on experience with diffusion models (image domain required; video preferred)

  • Experience with large scale multi-GPU / multi-node training

  • Good understanding of distributed training (DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed or similar)

  • Ability to design controlled experiments and interpret noisy results

Nice-to-have

  • Experience in avatar or human-centric generation

  • Familiarity with world / interactive models

  • Experience with GANs or VAEs

  • Python, PyTorch, CUDA

  • Sequence parallelism

  • AWS, SLURM, Docker

  • GitHub, CI/CD pipelines

title: Senior Infrastructure Manager
description: Who We Are At Partnerize, we're on a mission to transform the way businesses grow. We've built the leading partnership automation platform that empowers brands to discover, engage, and convert their audiences at scale. From affiliate marketing to influencer collaborations, we help our clients build and manage profitable partnerships that drive real results. We're a team of passionate problem-solvers who are dedicated to helping our clients win in the ever-evolving world of digital marketing. Why Join Us We're looking for passionate, talented people who want to be part of a winning team. At Partnerize, you'll find a culture of collaboration, innovation, and respect. We're guided by our core values, and we're committed to creating an environment where everyone can do their best work. We also offer a competitive salary, generous benefits, and a flexible work environment that allows you to thrive both personally and professionally. If you're ready to grow your career and make a difference, we'd love to hear from you. This role operates on a hybrid basis and requires attendance in our Newcastle office once a week. While some flexibility may be discussed, applicants should be willing and able to work from the office as part of the role.   The Role  We are looking for a Senior Infrastructure Manager who is, first and foremost, a people leader. In this role, your primary responsibility is the health, performance, and career growth of your engineering team. While you must possess a solid technical background to understand the challenges your team faces, your day-to-day focus will not be hands-on technical work. Instead, you will use your experience to remove blockers, guide decision-making, and ensure your engineers have the environment they need to succeed.   The Team You Will Lead  You will lead the Infrastructure Solutions team within the wider Technical Operations department. Your engineers are responsible for building the environment, delivering projects as requested by Engineering and Product, and ensuring we remain available, scalable, and secure. They are not responsible for the BAU function of the platforms that is managed by another team within Technical Operations. The Infrastructure Solutions team takes a concept or idea and makes that into a reality within the boundaries and constraints of our platforms.  You will be managing a team of engineers who individually possess experience in: On-Premise Linux systems, Container solutions, Debian packaging, Ansible, data streaming and queuing technologies such as Kafka or RabbitMQ Advanced database management knowledge (MySQL, Postgres) in replicated environments. Physical Network management, with an on-prem estate that is Juniper focused.  Cloud environments: GCP and AWS Platform engineer focused on building, maintaining and supporting an Internal Developer Platform (CI/CD)   The Operational Reality It is important to be transparent about the environment you are joining. We operate at high velocity with a broad and complex technology estate. However, we are a lean team, not a giant corporation with endless resources. Context Switching is the Norm You will rarely have the luxury of focusing on a single task for weeks at a time. You will be required to shift focus multiple times a week, and sometimes multiple times a day, as business priorities evolve. Agility over Silos Because we are a lean team, we wear many hats. You must be comfortable pivoting from a strategic discussion to an operational challenge without losing momentum. Focus Management Success in this role requires the ability to maintain high standards while navigating a workload that changes dynamically. This is not a role for those who prefer a slow, singular focus; it is for those who thrive on variety, pace, and solving complex problems in real-time.   As the Senior Infrastructure Manager, You Will: People Leadership & Talent Development Team Management Lead, mentor, and motivate a team of infrastructure engineers. Conduct weekly 1-2-1s, manage performance reviews, and handle all aspects of people management. Formal Training & Growth Go beyond ad-hoc mentoring to schedule and lead formal training sessions regarding operational improvements. Actively create professional development plans for your direct reports. Recruitment & Retention Own the hiring process for your team, ensuring we attract top talent and maintain a supportive, inclusive culture. Culture of Learning Foster a "Self-Learner" mindset. Create a transparent environment where failures are treated as learning opportunities and documented as such for future reference. Strategic & Operational Management Budget & Capacity Planning Ability to own your team's budget and lead capacity planning initiatives. You will forecast future infrastructure needs to ensure we remain scalable while managing spend for subscriptions and hardware. Risk & Contingency Proactively identify operational risks and form contingency plans immediately to ensure business continuity. Procedure & Frameworks Ability to define, maintain, and cascade operational procedures (SOPs) and ITIL standards. Prioritisation Shield your team from noise by effectively prioritising workloads (Changes, Problems, and Projects) and managing stakeholder expectations. Technical Support & Oversight Performance Optimisation Measure and optimise system performance with a focus on improving reliability and time-to-market. You will drive innovation to get ahead of internal customer needs rather than just reacting to them. Visual Documentation Ensure the team produces detailed system design documentation, specifically enforcing the inclusion of visual representations to support understanding. Ability to technologically assess it as a technical editor. Hybrid Estate Management Ability to oversee the management of both On-Premise and Cloud (GCP/AWS), ensuring high availability across all environments. Unblocking Issues Act as the senior escalation point for complex technical issues. Your goal is not to fix the issue yourself, but to coordinate the right resources and provide air cover. General Duties On-Call Duties Willingness to participate in the Management On-Call Rotation to support the department and the business (Current frequency: Once every three weeks). Ad-Hoc Carry out other strategic or technical duties required to support the Director/VP of Technical Operations. Essential Knowledge, Skills, and Experience Leadership & Management Competencies Proven Management Experience Significant experience leading a technical team, with a specific focus on the people management aspect (performance reviews, career growth etc). Project Management Strong project management experience with the ability to delegate effectively to meet tight deadlines. You must be able to multitask and maintain focus in a high-priority environment. Communication Exceptional verbal and written communication skills. You must be able to liaise effectively with management and other business areas. raw.title: Senior Infrastructure Manager
raw.description:
Who We Are

At Partnerize, we're on a mission to transform the way businesses grow. We've built the leading partnership automation platform that empowers brands to discover, engage, and convert their audiences at scale. From affiliate marketing to influencer collaborations, we help our clients build and manage profitable partnerships that drive real results. We're a team of passionate problem-solvers who are dedicated to helping our clients win in the ever-evolving world of digital marketing.

Why Join Us

We're looking for passionate, talented people who want to be part of a winning team. At Partnerize, you'll find a culture of collaboration, innovation, and respect. We're guided by our core values, and we're committed to creating an environment where everyone can do their best work. We also offer a competitive salary, generous benefits, and a flexible work environment that allows you to thrive both personally and professionally. If you're ready to grow your career and make a difference, we'd love to hear from you.

This role operates on a hybrid basis and requires attendance in our Newcastle office once a week. While some flexibility may be discussed, applicants should be willing and able to work from the office as part of the role.

 

The Role 

We are looking for a Senior Infrastructure Manager who is, first and foremost, a people leader.

In this role, your primary responsibility is the health, performance, and career growth of your engineering team. While you must possess a solid technical background to understand the challenges your team faces, your day-to-day focus will not be hands-on technical work. Instead, you will use your experience to remove blockers, guide decision-making, and ensure your engineers have the environment they need to succeed.

 

The Team You Will Lead 

You will lead the Infrastructure Solutions team within the wider Technical Operations department. Your engineers are responsible for building the environment, delivering projects as requested by Engineering and Product, and ensuring we remain available, scalable, and secure. They are not responsible for the BAU function of the platforms that is managed by another team within Technical Operations. The Infrastructure Solutions team takes a concept or idea and makes that into a reality within the boundaries and constraints of our platforms. 

You will be managing a team of engineers who individually possess experience in:

  • On-Premise Linux systems, Container solutions, Debian packaging, Ansible, data streaming and queuing technologies such as Kafka or RabbitMQ
  • Advanced database management knowledge (MySQL, Postgres) in replicated environments.
  • Physical Network management, with an on-prem estate that is Juniper focused. 
  • Cloud environments: GCP and AWS
  • Platform engineer focused on building, maintaining and supporting an Internal Developer Platform (CI/CD)

 

The Operational Reality

It is important to be transparent about the environment you are joining. We operate at high velocity with a broad and complex technology estate. However, we are a lean team, not a giant corporation with endless resources.

  • Context Switching is the Norm
    • You will rarely have the luxury of focusing on a single task for weeks at a time. You will be required to shift focus multiple times a week, and sometimes multiple times a day, as business priorities evolve.
  • Agility over Silos
    • Because we are a lean team, we wear many hats. You must be comfortable pivoting from a strategic discussion to an operational challenge without losing momentum.
  • Focus Management
    • Success in this role requires the ability to maintain high standards while navigating a workload that changes dynamically. This is not a role for those who prefer a slow, singular focus; it is for those who thrive on variety, pace, and solving complex problems in real-time.

 

As the Senior Infrastructure Manager, You Will:

People Leadership & Talent Development

  • Team Management
    • Lead, mentor, and motivate a team of infrastructure engineers. Conduct weekly 1-2-1s, manage performance reviews, and handle all aspects of people management.
  • Formal Training & Growth
    • Go beyond ad-hoc mentoring to schedule and lead formal training sessions regarding operational improvements. Actively create professional development plans for your direct reports.
  • Recruitment & Retention
    • Own the hiring process for your team, ensuring we attract top talent and maintain a supportive, inclusive culture.
  • Culture of Learning
    • Foster a "Self-Learner" mindset. Create a transparent environment where failures are treated as learning opportunities and documented as such for future reference.

Strategic & Operational Management

  • Budget & Capacity Planning
    • Ability to own your team's budget and lead capacity planning initiatives. You will forecast future infrastructure needs to ensure we remain scalable while managing spend for subscriptions and hardware.
  • Risk & Contingency
    • Proactively identify operational risks and form contingency plans immediately to ensure business continuity.
  • Procedure & Frameworks
    • Ability to define, maintain, and cascade operational procedures (SOPs) and ITIL standards.
  • Prioritisation
    • Shield your team from noise by effectively prioritising workloads (Changes, Problems, and Projects) and managing stakeholder expectations.

Technical Support & Oversight

  • Performance Optimisation
    • Measure and optimise system performance with a focus on improving reliability and time-to-market. You will drive innovation to get ahead of internal customer needs rather than just reacting to them.
  • Visual Documentation
    • Ensure the team produces detailed system design documentation, specifically enforcing the inclusion of visual representations to support understanding. Ability to technologically assess it as a technical editor.
  • Hybrid Estate Management
    • Ability to oversee the management of both On-Premise and Cloud (GCP/AWS), ensuring high availability across all environments.
  • Unblocking Issues
    • Act as the senior escalation point for complex technical issues. Your goal is not to fix the issue yourself, but to coordinate the right resources and provide air cover.

General Duties

On-Call DutiesWillingness to participate in the Management On-Call Rotation to support the department and the business (Current frequency: Once every three weeks). Ad-HocCarry out other strategic or technical duties required to support the Director/VP of Technical Operations.

Essential Knowledge, Skills, and Experience

Leadership & Management Competencies

  • Proven Management Experience
    • Significant experience leading a technical team, with a specific focus on the people management aspect (performance reviews, career growth etc).
  • Project Management
    • Strong project management experience with the ability to delegate effectively to meet tight deadlines. You must be able to multitask and maintain focus in a high-priority environment.
  • Communication
    • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills. You must be able to liaise effectively with management and other business areas. Engagement may also include interactions with senior technical engineers/leaders within other teams and C-Team members. 
  • Goal Oriented
    • You must be highly goal-oriented with strict attention to detail, capable of prioritising workload and demand to ensure targets are met.
  • ITIL Application / Lean Six Sigma
    • Deep knowledge of and experience with ITIL practices, with the ability to apply them to improve team workflows. Demonstrated ability to apply Lean Six Sigma concepts.

 

Technical Environment & Team Capabilities

Focusing on the technical skills that your engineers possess, it would be ideal if you had a decent working knowledge of each of the areas. Hands-on expertise in every area is not required, but the ability to hold and facilitate discussions, know when to push or hold back and when to ask poignant questions will help you effectively mentor the team and guide architectural decisions. 

For reference from above these areas are: on-prem and AWS/GCP solutions; system design from network to application level; resilient database availability strategies; automation and configuration management via Ansible, Docker and CI/CD; programming awareness in Python; Linux administration.

Your willingness to learn what you don't know is required to succeed in this role and we will support you through that journey.

 

Desirable Knowledge, Skills, and Experience

The following skills or experiences are advantageous but not strictly required. They would be utilised for facilitating tasks rather than for direct, hands-on implementation.

  • Innovation & Debt Management
    • A keen interest in new technologies and innovation, specifically supporting development teams in the refactoring of technical debt.
  • Advanced Containerization
    • Deep knowledge of Kubernetes, Docker, and container ecosystems.
  • Observability
    • Experience with monitoring systems (e.g., Zabbix, Grafana) and logging stacks (Elasticsearch, Kibana).
  • Data Streaming
    • Experience with data streaming and queuing technologies, specifically Apache Kafka and Druid.
  • Web & Storage
    • Knowledge of Nginx (or other web server technologies) and storage technologies like Gluster.
  • Tooling
    • Proficiency with JIRA and Confluence for project tracking and documentation.
  • Version Control
    • strong understanding of Git and version control best practices.

 

Why This Role?

If you are an experienced technical leader who finds more satisfaction in growing people and building high-performing teams than in closing tickets yourself, this is the role for you. You will have the autonomy to shape the culture of the Infrastructure function and the strategic backing to make a real impact on the business

 

UK Benefits & Perks

  • 25 days holiday in addition to bank holidays 
  • Enhanced Parental Leave: 6 months full pay for birth parent, 4 weeks non-birth parent at full pay after one year employment
  • 5 extra 'Partnerize Parental Days' each year
  • Private Medical Insurance through Vitality 
  • Enhanced pension contributions
  • Cycle to Work scheme 
  • Eye Care Vouchers 
  • Life Assurance
  • Enhanced Wellness Program including access to EAP, Wellness Coaching & Wellness Fridays program
  • Regular company events and activities

Our Commitment to Diversity & Inclusion

We are committed to attracting, developing, and advancing our outstanding team members, regardless of race, ethnic identity, sexual orientation, religion, age, gender, gender identity, physical abilities, or any other dimension of diversity. We strive to foster an environment where people can be their authentic selves, raise concerns and innovate, all without fear; where they are treated fairly and respectfully, have equal access to opportunities and resources and can contribute fully to the organization's success. Every individual in our business is expected to live this commitment without exception.

Privacy and data protection. The data collected as part of this application will be used for the recruitment process and any subsequent employment. You can find further information in Partnerize privacy policy here: https://partnerize.com/privacy-policy/
